message.content:
Based on the image, here is a description of the **death/jumpscare screen** elements:

## Visual Elements
- **Animatronic Face**: A close-up of a stylized, cartoonish face dominates the center featuring:
  - **Glowing eyes**: Two bright, glowing green oval eyes with a soft blur/glow effect
  - **Grinning mouth**: A wide, unnerving smile composed of horizontal black and white/cream stripes (resembling a barcode or teeth)
  - The face appears to be floating or superimposed over a dark background

## Background & Atmosphere
- **Setting**: A dark, ominous corridor or room with a **checkered floor** (black and white tiles) visible beneath the face
- **Lighting**: Heavy vignette effect with deep red/brown shadows at the edges, creating a claustrophobic, threatening atmosphere
- **Texture**: Grainy/noisy overlay suggesting old surveillance footage or VHS quality

## UI Text Elements
- **Top Center (Instruction Box)**: 
  - *"HAZ CLIC PARA CAPTURAR EL RATÓN — o mantén clic y arrastra para mirar"*
  - (Spanish for: "CLICK TO CAPTURE THE MOUSE — or hold click and drag to look")
  
- **Left Side (Partial Text)**: 
  - Faint, barely visible text that appears to say something like:
    - *"...tabierta"*
    - *"...de raqueta"*
    - *"...icina"*
    - *"...e vigilancia"*
  - (Suggesting "Puerta abierta", "Sala de raqueta", "Oficina", "Cámara de vigilancia")

## Game Interface
- **Bottom Left**: A red notification badge showing **"N 1 Issue ×"** — suggesting this is a debug/development build or the player has triggered an error/state

## Notable Absences
Unlike traditional FNAF-style death screens, this image **does not show**:
- A "GAME OVER" or "MUERTE/CAUGHT" title
- Retry/Continue buttons
- A "Press Space to Continue" prompt
- Static/fuzz overlay (though it has grain)

**Overall Impression**: This appears to be either the **moment of jumpscare impact** (before the game over screen loads) or a **custom/indie horror game** death state with a minimalist, creepy aesthetic reminiscent of *Poppy Playtime* or *The Mandela Catalogue* style horror. The striped smile and glowing green eyes create an uncanny, "wrong" feeling typical of analog horror.
